doc.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Composers outlast performers: Ellington, Tatum, Nat Cole
summary: Williams says composers are remembered more than performers and notes Duke's bedside piano; Peterson agrees about Tatum.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Edward used to keep — Duke — he kept a piano beside the bed, a little, oh what are those things?

No, no not a Fender Rhodes, the other one that they used to play all the time, I’ve forgotten the name of them now. But he kept that little thing right beside his bed, and paper, right here by his left hand, so that he could come right out of his bed and do it, or didn’t have to get out of the bed to do it.

And these things that are given to us to do. I am so pleased that you are writing and I’ll tell you why. Rozelle Gail, who is a good friend of Art Tatum, you know, and he used to beg Art to write. And Art he says, “I’ll write it down for you, don’t worry.” “But you should write” [grumbles] “I don’t want to write.”
You’re caught up in the playing.
But the thing is, they’ll remember composers. Composers are remembered much more so than performing artists.
The records won’t be played, we won’t hear — I haven’t heard an Art Tatum recording on the radio, not even on a jazz station, in I don’t know how long.
I know. And it’s a shame.

And same thing with a performer like Nat King Cole. Every now and then you’ll hear a Nat King Cole record. But they didn’t compose anything. And I’m so pleased that you are, because that will last. Writing always lasts.

Yeah, it outlasts the players. Unfortunately, but it does. You know people today will recognize Tchaikovsky, they’ll recognize Ellington, you know, but if you play them an Art Tatum record, they wouldn’t know what you’re talking about many times. Or it could be a Dizzy.
And it’s as fresh today as it was the date that they did it. Just as fresh. Their music today is just as fresh and beautiful and inspiring — and awe inspiring rather.
